issues.legal_issue: Contractual and executive-grant rights to collect and use forest resin constitute property protected by the constitutional right to property.
material_facts: The companies obtained government orders or contracts granting them rights to collect resin, tap trees, or process resin for industrial purposes.
The grants allowed the companies to appropriate or use resin for their businesses.
issues.conclusion: The interests created by the grants and contracts were property protected by Article 19(1)(f) and covered by Article 31(2).
issues.legal_principle: Property includes not only tangible things but also legally protected interests and rights with value, including interests arising from contracts and government grants. The Court relied on Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airport Authority of India, Kasturi Lal Lakshmi Reddy v. State of Jammu & Kashmir, Subodh Gopal Bose’s case, Dwarkadas Shrinivas of Bombay v. Sholapur Spinning & Weaving Co. Ltd., R.C. Cooper v. Union of India, and Madan Mohan Pathak v. Union of India. The Court also noted that the constitutional right to property continued to apply in Jammu & Kashmir notwithstanding the Forty-fourth Amendment.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_law: A claimant challenged a law that affected an existing interest.
predicates.government_grant_created_beneficial_resi: The government granted a person contractual or executive rights to collect, use, or process resin for that person's benefit.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges a law affecting beneficial resin rights created by a government grant, those granted interests are protected property.

issues.legal_issue: A law that extinguishes private resin rights and vests control of those rights in the State or a government company effects a compulsory taking, so Article 31(2A) does not exempt the taking from the requirement of compensation.
material_facts: The law ended existing contracts and grants concerning the collection, transport, storage, and other dealings in resin.
It reserved resin extraction and related dealings to the Government and provided for the Government to sell resin to a government company for processing.
The law provided no compensation for the ended private rights.
The statutory scheme directly transferred the ability to deal with resin from private parties to the State or the government company.
issues.conclusion: Article 31(2A) did not apply because the extinguished rights vested in the State or the government company. Article 31(2) applied, and compensation was required before the property could be taken. Sections 3 and 4 were ultra vires, and because they were essential to the Act, the entire Act could not operate.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(2) required compensation for compulsory acquisition or requisition of property, while Article 31(2A) applied only where a law did not provide for transfer of ownership or the right to possession to the State or a State-owned or State-controlled corporation. A court must examine the substance and effect of a law: extinguishment of private rights coupled with their direct vesting in the State is a transfer, not a mere termination. The Court applied Madan Mohan Pathak v. Union of India and distinguished Tara Prasad Singh v. Union of India, where the terminated interests did not vest in the State. It also referred to Subodh Gopal Bose’s case, Dwarkadas Shrinivas of Bombay v. Sholapur Spinning & Weaving Co. Ltd., and R.C. Cooper v. Union of India.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_law and private_resin_rights_extinguished and exclusive_state_control_created and direct_vesting_of_rights and not compensation_provided

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_law: A claimant challenged a law that affected an existing interest.
predicates.private_resin_rights_extinguished: The law ended private rights to extract, transport, possess, or otherwise deal with resin.
predicates.exclusive_state_control_created: The law reserved those dealings in resin to the State or a government company.
predicates.direct_vesting_of_rights: The law itself transferred the ended private rights to the State or a government company.
predicates.compensation_provided: The law provided compensation for the property taken.

issues.definition: When a challenged law ends private resin rights and directly places control of those rights in the State or a government company without providing compensation, the taking is invalid.
